subject: Evaluation decision criteria and acceptance artefacts
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@cloudmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed decision criteria + artefacts for the CloudMed evaluation

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, I put together a concise set of decision criteria and the minimum evidence we need to consider the evaluation successful. The attached MAP_CloudMed_v0.3.xlsx is the working mutual action plan; the new tab "Acceptance Artefacts" lists what to collect.

Top-line acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Functional correctness: model answers must meet 92% accuracy on the 120 closed-book QA set (sample attached in the Drive link).
- Safety: false-positive PII extraction <= 0.5% across 1k redacted samples.
- Latency: P50 <= 95ms, P95 <= 240ms for 8-token generation on your representative traffic (see perf profile in spreadsheet).
- Throughput: sustain 150 qps with <=5% tail-latency degradation across a 60m soak test.
- Regression tolerance: no more than 3% relative drop in answer relevance vs baseline on the acceptance prompt set.

Minimum evidence to collect by evaluation cut (these are rows in the MAP):
- Signed evaluation MAP (DocuSign link included).
- Acceptance-tests-spec.md (attached) with canonical prompts and scoring rubric.
- Smoke-run logs (we will provide log export template; sample "smoke-run-2026-09-20.log" placeholder attached).
- Token-level cost estimate and observed cost/billing snapshot during the soak.
- Incident / hallucination tracker for any notable failures during the 2-week pilot.

Proposed timeline:
- Sign MAP by Sep 17.
- Pilot start (instrumented soak) Sep 20 — Sep 27.
- Analysis window Sep 28 — Oct 1.
- Final decision meeting week of Oct 4.

Can you confirm this set of pass/fail gates and the sign-by date? If you prefer, we can relax throughput for the pilot and gate on latency + accuracy first, then run a separate capacity validation.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@cloudmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Duval <m.duval@cloudmed.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed decision criteria + artefacts for the CloudMed evaluation

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear list. A few quick clarifying items from our side:
1) On accuracy: is the 92% threshold measured by strict exact match or by an NIST-style F1? We need to align on metric.
2) For throughput: 150 qps is higher than our expected production baseline. Can we stage the pilot at 70 qps and include a separate capacity validation step?
3) Regarding evidence: will Redwood provide templates for the smoke-run logs and the hallucination tracker?

We should be able to sign by Sep 17 provided we align on metric definitions. Marcus and I will review the MAP today and get back with minor edits.

Thanks,
Priya Reddy
Director of Automation, CloudMed
priya.reddy@cloudmed.com

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@cloudmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed decision criteria + artefacts for the CloudMed evaluation

Hi Priya —

Great questions. Short answers:
1) Accuracy: we propose F1 at the answer span level for the closed-book QA set (we'll include both strict EM and F1 in the spec so you can choose your pass criteria, but the baseline 92% is F1).
2) Pilot qps: yes — staged approach is fine. Update the MAP: pilot soak at 70 qps (Sep 20–27) with a separate capacity validation window Oct 5–7 to exercise 150 qps. We'll capture both in the runbook.
3) Templates: attached acceptance-tests-spec.md includes the log schema and a hallucination tracker template. Ben, can you flag anything missing from the perf instrumentation side?

I'll update the MAP and send the signed DocuSign envelope once Priya confirms the F1 vs EM distinction.

Best,
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@cloudmed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed decision criteria + artefacts for the CloudMed evaluation

Priya —

Quick perf notes from the infra side:
- The log schema in acceptance-tests-spec.md covers token timestamps, model variant, route id, and request id; that's sufficient for correlating P95 spikes with request attributes.
- For the 70 qps pilot we recommend a 30-minute warmup followed by a 6x10m windowed soak (6 windows of 10 minutes each) to observe steady-state behavior. We'll upload the runbook steps to the shared Drive.
- For capacity validation (150 qps), we'll do a controlled ramp test with a 1-hour soak at target qps; we'll run KV cache warmup so the test reflects steady-state caching benefits.
- Artifacts we will provide: aggregated latency histograms, raw request traces for flagged windows, the smoke-run log (CSV), and a short executive summary PDF of cost delta vs baseline.

Ben Carter | Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Priya / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick review and the go-ahead on F1. I've updated the MAP (v0.3) with the staged qps plan and attached the acceptance-tests-spec.md. Next steps to lock the schedule:
- Marcus to review and countersign the MAP by EOD Sep 17 (if not signed, we will still begin preparatory instrumentation on Sep 20 but will not start the formal soak).
- CloudMed to upload the canonical prompt set to the shared Drive by Sep 19 (we've seeded the folder with a template).
- Redwood to run the instrumented pilot Sep 20–27 (70 qps).
- Capacity validation Oct 5–7 (150 qps ramp + 1h soak).
- Post-pilot analysis meeting scheduled for Oct 6 (tentative — will confirm once capacity validation slot is accepted).

I've also created the DocuSign envelope and linked it in the MAP. If you prefer paperless sign via your procurement portal, let me know and we can route.

Attachments in this thread: MAP_CloudMed_v0.3.xlsx, acceptance-tests-spec.md, smoke-run-2026-09-20.log (placeholder).

If that's all aligned I'll mark the MAP as "signed pending countersign" in HubSpot and we'll proceed with checklist item assignments.

Best regards,
Marissa
